title: Proper/open exchange for one cartesian refinement
statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring, a:V→X and j:U→Y open immersions, and sq:a≫f=p≫j a cartesian square of schemes. Let c,d be compactifications of f, r:c.Refinement d a proper refinement, and hr:IsPullback c.i id_X r.hom d.i. Its literal pullback rU=r.ofIsPullback sq is a refinement cU→dU with cartesian source square hrU. Write ρ(r) and ρ(rU) for the specified derived unit/inverse-open-base-change/proper-composition refinement maps of [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and P(c),P(d) for [def-asd-open-support-pullback-model]. Then (ρ(rU) ▷ Dj!) ≫ P(c).hom = P(d).hom ≫ (Da! ◁ ρ(r)). This involves only one supplied refinement and its literal pullback; no graph comparison, common refinement, density, or quasi-compactness is assumed.

source.place: Coherences (i) and (iii): restriction of the compactification diagram to an open and adjunction transposition.

proof.text: Construct the explicit triangles (p,j) and (a,f), with common output c.precomp a, and likewise for d. The first uses c.ofIsPullback sq and the trivial open compactification of j; the second uses the trivial open compactification of a and c. The map r.hom gives their output refinements. Their source cartesian squares follow from hr and its literal pullback, including the precomposition of hr by a. Thus r and r.ofIsPullback sq define the two triangle morphisms used by the proof.

Use the existing arbitrary-scheme unboundedFormalism implementation, unbounded_has_base_change, unbounded_has_proper_exchange, and CompactSupportFormalism.compIso_naturality on both triangle morphisms. Remove the identity proper pushforwards attached to the trivial open compactifications by pfId. Identity-refinement comparison is the identity. Naturality of pfId then gives the naturality equations for the two normalized triangle compositions.

Compute the normalized (a,f) compositor using identity-horizontal exchange and the left identity proper compositor. It is the inverse open compositor whiskered by proper direct image. Compute the normalized (p,j) compositor using compIso_hom_app and the right identity proper compositor. Package their exchange/open-compositor factors in a generic raw comparison; its composite with the normalized (a,f) compositor is the normalized (p,j) compositor, by functoriality and cancellation of the open-composition isomorphism. Use unbounded_open_exchange and unbounded_sh_comp, including congruence under the pullback open equation, to identify this generic raw comparison with P(c). Thus P(c) followed by the first normalized compositor is the second; likewise for d.

The existing unbounded_refinement_comparison identifies all formalism refinement maps with the specified unit/inverse-open-base-change/proper-composition maps. Substitute the factorization into the two normalized triangle-naturality equations, which have the same output refinement. Reassociate and cancel the normalized (a,f) composition isomorphism for c. This is the displayed single-refinement equation; the construction uses no quasi-compactness of the opens or Noetherian hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Coherence (i), proved using two explicit triangles and the existing general compIso_naturality theorem. The private unboundedFormalism, exchange, open-compositor and refinement identifications are all arbitrary-scheme constructions, despite the Noetherian hypotheses on some public theorems in their module.

theorem openSupportPullbackIso_refinement
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {X Y U V : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {j : U ⟶ Y} [IsOpenImmersion j] {a : V ⟶ X} [IsOpenImmersion a]
    {p : V ⟶ U} (sq : IsPullback a p f j)
    {c d : Compactification f} (r : c.Refinement d)
    (hr : IsPullback c.i (𝟙 X) r.hom d.i) :
    Functor.whiskerRight
        (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationComparison (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)
          (r.ofIsPullback sq) (r.isPullback_ofIsPullback sq hr))
        D((j)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ]) ≫
      (openSupportPullbackIso Λ sq c).hom =
    (openSupportPullbackIso Λ sq d).hom ≫
      Functor.whiskerLeft D((a)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])
        (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationComparison (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)
          r hr)
